story: A pending FERC preliminary permit application for a 100 MW subsea AI data center on a 1,650 acre operational envelope of Cook Inlet seabed west of Nikiski has opened no public comment period in Alaska, while the same company's Maine twin was cut by roughly 70 percent and frozen by a unanimous 180 day Eastport moratorium

claims.claim: A Federal Register full text search for DeepGreen returned zero documents when checked on August 21st, 2026, so FERC has published no notice accepting the Cook Inlet application for filing.
claims.verbatim: {"description":"Documents matching 'DeepGreen'","count":0}
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register API, Office of the Federal Register
claims.notes: The run's central primary fact. Two scouts and the fact-checker each got 0 independently. It proves no notice soliciting comments has been PUBLISHED, which is the step that opens a comment period. It does NOT prove the application does not exist and the deck must never say so.

claims.claim: The same Federal Register search returns seven documents for the term Cook Inlet hydrokinetic, so the zero result for DeepGreen is not a failure of the search.
claims.verbatim: Documents matching 'Cook Inlet hydrokinetic'
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register API, Office of the Federal Register
claims.notes: The control that makes C01 meaningful. Without it the absence is just a query that did not work.

claims.claim: FERC published a notice accepting Ocean Renewable Power Company's Cook Inlet preliminary permit application for filing and soliciting comments on May 11, 2021, under Project No. 15116-000.
claims.verbatim: Ocean Renewable Power Company, Inc.; Notice of Preliminary Permit Application Accepted for Filing and Soliciting Comments, Motions To Intervene, and Competing Applications
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission via Federal Register
claims.notes: The docket_ids field returns exactly Project No. 15116-000. This is the shape of document that is missing for DeepGreen.

claims.claim: FERC published an Ocean Renewable Power Company Notice of Intent to File License Application soliciting comments on April 8, 2025, under Project No. 15116-001.
claims.verbatim: "publication_date": "2025-04-08", "docket_ids": ["Project No. 15116-001"]
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission via Federal Register
claims.notes: Second proof that Cook Inlet hydrokinetic notices do reach the Federal Register and do solicit comment.

claims.claim: FERC published a Littoral Power Systems notice of preliminary permit application accepted for filing on September 12, 2023.
claims.verbatim: Littoral Power Systems, Inc.; Notice of Preliminary Permit Application Accepted for Filing
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission via Federal Register
claims.notes: Third control document. No P number confirmed from the title, so the deck must not assert one for it.

claims.claim: Ocean Renewable Power Company's East Foreland Tidal Energy Project is sited in Cook Inlet near Nikiski and adjacent lands of the Kenai Peninsula Borough.
claims.verbatim: Cook Inlet near Nikiski and adjacent lands of the Kenai Peninsula Borough, Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission via Federal Register
claims.notes: Same waters as the DeepGreen proposal, which is what makes the scale comparison fair.

claims.claim: The East Foreland tidal project's total capacity is 1.98 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: The proposed East Foreland project's total capacity is slated for 1.98 megawatts
claims.source_outlet: Peninsula Clarion and Homer News, Delcenia Cosman
claims.notes: Corroborated arithmetically by the primary FERC filing in C08. Background source, older than the window, and labelled as background wherever used.

claims.claim: ORPC's East Foreland pilot as described to FERC consists of a 1.75 megawatt Proteus Marine Renewables AR1750 tidal device and a 0.23 megawatt ORPC TidGen80 device.
claims.verbatim: a 1.75-megawatt (MW) Proteus Marine Renewables AR1750 tidal device
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission via Federal Register
claims.notes: 1.75 plus 0.23 equals 1.98, which independently confirms C07. The sum is arithmetic, so the 1.98 figure is attributed to the Peninsula Clarion.

claims.claim: ORPC's 2021 Cook Inlet preliminary permit application described turbine generator units with a combined capacity of no more than 5 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: A series of proprietary turbine-generator units with a combined capacity of no more than 5 megawatts
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission via Federal Register
claims.notes: The stage-matched comparison, and the strongest one in the deck. The ceiling ORPC set for itself at the SAME permit stage in the SAME inlet was 5 MW. DeepGreen's permit-stage figure is 100 MW.

claims.claim: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC has proposed a 100 megawatt underwater data center project off the shore of Nikiski.
claims.verbatim: Delaware-based DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC released plans for a 100-megawatt data center project
claims.notes: In window. ADN attributes the specifications to FERC filings it reviewed.

claims.claim: The proposal includes 66 hives housing AI servers, both powered and cooled by the water of Cook Inlet.
claims.verbatim: 66 "hives" housing AI servers, both powered and cooled by water of Cook Inlet
claims.notes: FERC's own deficiency letter uses the term subsea-compute hives per C20, which corroborates the term if not the count.

claims.claim: The February filing for the Cook Inlet project proposed approximately 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines using the company's proprietary Universal Docking Cradle system.
claims.verbatim: approximately 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines using the company's proprietary Universal Docking Cradle system
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: Conflict settled in favour of the range. ADN prints as many 350 underwater turbines, apparently a typo for as many as 350, which is a ceiling rather than a count. Never print a flat 350.

claims.claim: The February filing proposed an initial operational envelope of 1,650 acres in Cook Inlet.
claims.verbatim: The February filing for DeepGreen Cook Inlet SVP proposed an initial operational envelope of 1,650 acres
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: The outlet prints SVP rather than SPV in this sentence. ADN independently corroborates the acreage. The word ENVELOPE is load bearing and must survive into the deck, because an envelope is the area asked for and not the footprint built, which is exactly the distinction FERC pressed in Maine per C40.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet project corridor lies west of the Nikiski shoreline in water 45 feet to 166 feet deep.
claims.verbatim: an approximately 1,650-acre corridor in the Cook Inlet west of the Nikiski shoreline, with depths ranging from 45 feet to 166 feet
claims.notes: Also independently corroborates the 1,650 acre figure in C13.

claims.claim: DeepGreen estimated the preliminary engineering studies at 4.5 million dollars and expects them to take four years.
claims.verbatim: DeepGreen estimated preliminary engineering studies, expected to take four years to complete, to cost $4.5 million, according to FERC filings.
claims.notes: Four years matches the statutory maximum term of a preliminary permit in C45, which is a useful internal consistency check.

claims.claim: The applicant is DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, a Delaware based entity, and its parent DeepGreen Holdings LLC formed in January, one month before the FERC application was sent.
claims.verbatim: DeepGreen Cook Inlet's parent company, DeepGreen Holdings LLC, formed in January, one month before Wolfson sent in an application to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
claims.notes: January means January 2026 and the application therefore lands in February 2026, matching The Maine Monitor's February filing. ADN also reports the company uses Delaware incorporation partly because the state's laws allow a lack of ownership disclosure information.

claims.claim: Louis Wolfson, a managing member for DeepGreen Cook Inlet, is a luxury real estate developer based in Needham, Massachusetts.
claims.verbatim: said Louis Wolfson, a managing member for DeepGreen Cook Inlet and luxury real estate developer based in Needham, Massachusetts
claims.notes: Single sourced, and it is the applicant's own named principal speaking to the outlet.

claims.claim: Wolfson said land based data centers face major constraints because they take up large plots of real estate, strain local power grids, and consume millions of gallons of fresh water daily for cooling.
claims.verbatim: land-based data centers face major constraints because they take up large plots of real estate, strain local power grids, and consume millions of gallons of fresh water daily for cooling
claims.notes: This is the applicant's pitch, not a verified engineering finding. Present it as what Wolfson said.

claims.claim: The proposal describes silt protection scour skirts engineered to protect the infrastructure from the harsh tides.
claims.verbatim: Silt-protection "scour skirts" have been engineered to protect the infrastructure from the harsh tides.
claims.notes: Use the page's own form. The phrase engineered scour skirts as such does not appear.

claims.claim: A June 18th letter from FERC's Northwest Branch Division of Hydropower Licensing found DeepGreen failed to provide the dimensions and physical composition of many of the data center's underwater infrastructure components.
claims.verbatim: according to a June 18 letter from the Northwest Branch Division of Hydropower Licensing
claims.notes: This is the ALASKA letter and it is a different letter from the Maine one in C38. Different date, different branch. The named components on the page are an underwater platform, subsea-compute hives and silt protection systems. ADN publishes NO COUNT of Alaska deficiencies, so the deck must never say three.

claims.claim: FERC also found that DeepGreen did not notify the City of Kenai and failed to identify all tribes and Alaska Native corporations that may have interest in or be affected by the project.
claims.verbatim: DeepGreen did not notify the City of Kenai and failed to identify all tribes and Alaska Native corporations that may have interest in or be affected by the project, according to the commission.
claims.notes: The 15 mile radius and population over 5,000 threshold that scouts attached to this does NOT appear on the page and is killed.

claims.claim: DeepGreen corrected its mistakes in a letter sent a week later.
claims.verbatim: DeepGreen corrected its mistakes in a letter sent a week later.
claims.notes: The page says a week later, not an exact date. Do not compute June 25th and print it.

claims.claim: FERC spokesperson Celeste Miller said that after staff determine the application is complete, the commission will request comments from the public.
claims.verbatim: After staff determine the application is complete, the commission will request comments from the public, she said.
claims.notes: The hinge of the story. The commission's own spokesperson says the comment period comes AFTER completeness. Read with C01 this claim carries the deck.

claims.claim: Alaska Energy Authority CEO Curtis Thayer said the organization had never heard of DeepGreen nor received any contact from the company.
claims.verbatim: Alaska Energy Authority CEO Curtis Thayer said the organization had never heard of DeepGreen nor received any contact from the company.
claims.notes: Load bearing, because DeepGreen's filing names AEA's PowerLink as its interconnection. See C28.

claims.claim: Thayer said it is extremely disappointing that they would send something to FERC without contacting us.
claims.verbatim: It's extremely disappointing that they would send something to FERC without contacting us,
claims.notes: Verified verbatim including the contraction.

claims.claim: Thayer said DeepGreen's letter to FERC has some of the project's facts dead wrong.
claims.verbatim: Thayer said DeepGreen's letter to FERC also has some of the project's facts "dead wrong."
claims.notes: Only the two words dead wrong are inside quotation marks on the page. The page does not say WHICH facts, so the deck must not imply the PowerLink cost is the error.

claims.claim: Kenai City Manager Terry Eubank said he does not know that it would be any more substantial than the oil and gas production out there, but he thinks it always has to be examined and looked at.
claims.value: oil and gas production out there
claims.verbatim: I don't know that it'd be any more substantial than (the) oil and gas production out there, but I think it always has to be examined and looked at,
claims.notes: ADN also reports Eubank made city councilors aware of the project during their August meeting as the city was recently noticed, which is the practical consequence of the notification deficiency in C21.

claims.claim: DeepGreen told FERC its project is designed to tie in with the Alaska Energy Authority's Cook Inlet PowerLink project, a 38 mile submarine transmission line planned between Nikiski and Beluga.
claims.verbatim: DeepGreen said its project is designed to tie in with the Alaska Energy Authority's ongoing $400 million Cook Inlet PowerLink project, a 38-mile submarine transmission line planned between Nikiski and Beluga.
claims.notes: TRAP CLAIM. The $400 million inside this verbatim conflicts with AEA's own published $142 Million in C29. The deck must NOT state the PowerLink cost as one settled number.

claims.claim: The Alaska Energy Authority's own project page states the total Cook Inlet PowerLink project cost is 142 million dollars.
claims.verbatim: $142 Million
claims.notes: PRIMARY, and it disagrees with the reporting figure in C28. AEA's page carries no visible publication date so date_of_source is the fetch date.

claims.claim: The Alaska Energy Authority describes Cook Inlet PowerLink as a 38 mile subsea cable delivering up to 200 megawatts of bidirectional power transfer.
claims.verbatim: deliver up to 200 megawatts of bidirectional power transfer
claims.notes: The page also prints 38-mile subsea cable, matching ADN's 38 miles exactly. State the two numbers, 100 and 200, and let the reader do the division. Do not print a percentage AEA has not published.

claims.claim: The Alaska Energy Authority lists the Cook Inlet PowerLink project status as In Development and funded for 8 years.
claims.verbatim: Status: In Development
claims.notes: The cable DeepGreen proposes to plug into is not built.

claims.claim: DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC submitted its Maine preliminary permit application to FERC on February 11th, seeking a 48 month permit.
claims.verbatim: DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC submitted an application to FERC on February 11 for a preliminary permit
claims.notes: CONFLICT SETTLED. February 11th is the MAINE filing date and only the Maine one. No source gives a day for the Alaska filing, only February. The deck must not say the two were filed the same day.

claims.claim: The Maine project as originally filed was a 51 megawatt tidal energy and subsea data center with 170 turbines, estimated to cost 415 million dollars.
claims.verbatim: The project is estimated to cost $415 million
claims.notes: 51 MW and 170 turbines are corroborated independently by The Maine Monitor. The 415 million dollar figure is single sourced.

claims.claim: The original Maine filing sought 400 acres while its active infrastructure would occupy about 27 acres, roughly 7 percent of the space.
claims.verbatim: Seeking permit for 400 acres, with active infrastructure occupying about 27 acres (approximately 7% of the space)
claims.notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT CATCH OF THE RUN. The February filing ALREADY described about 27 acres of active infrastructure inside a 400 acre envelope. So a 400 to 27.1 comparison is an envelope against a footprint and is NOT a 94 percent cut in anything physical. Any slide claiming that is wrong and must not be built.

claims.claim: DeepGreen told FERC the Maine project's total proposed operational capacity has been scaled down to a maximum of 15 megawatts, against an earlier proposal that envisioned up to 51 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: total proposed project operational capacity has been scaled down to a maximum of 15 MW (megawatts) to align with revised commercial modeling,
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: The company's own words quoted from its FERC filing. 51 to 15 is a reduction of about 70 percent, and that is the honest headline number for the Maine cut.

claims.claim: In the revised Maine Phase I DeepGreen projects installing 16 marine hydrokinetic turbines, increasing to 34 in Phase II, against approximately 170 in the original application.
claims.verbatim: In the revised Phase I, DeepGreen projects installing 16 marine hydrokinetic turbines, increasing to 34 in Phase II.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: 16 plus 34 is 50, against approximately 170, a reduction of about 70 percent that matches the capacity cut in C35 almost exactly. Whether 34 is cumulative or additional is not stated, so hedge if the deck sums them.

claims.claim: In July DeepGreen amended its Maine proposal, scaling back Phase I from 15 megawatts to 1 to 5 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: In July, DeepGreen amended its proposal to dramatically cut the project's energy consumption, scaling back Phase I from 15 megawatts to 1 to 5 megawatts
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: CONFLICT SETTLED. The page says In July with no day. The June 8th amendment date one scout reported is unsupported and is killed.

claims.claim: In a July 15th letter FERC requested more information from DeepGreen after finding four deficiencies in its Maine preliminary permit application.
claims.verbatim: In a July 15 letter, FERC requested more information from DeepGreen after finding four deficiencies in its preliminary permit application.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: CONFLICT SETTLED. This is the MAINE letter, July 15th, four deficiencies. C20 is the ALASKA letter, June 18th, Northwest branch, count not published. Never merge them.

claims.claim: Emily Carter, chief of FERC's New England branch in the Division of Hydropower Licensing, gave DeepGreen 45 days to respond.
claims.verbatim: Emily Carter, chief of FERC's New England branch in the Division of Hydropower Licensing, gave DeepGreen 45 days to respond.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: New England branch for Maine against Northwest branch for Alaska in C20. The branch names are the cleanest proof these are two distinct letters.

claims.claim: One of the four Maine deficiencies was the lack of a detailed technical explanation for requesting a 400 acre operational envelope when the active infrastructure footprint is significantly smaller.
claims.verbatim: Lack of a detailed technical explanation for requesting a 400-acre 'operational envelope' when the active infrastructure footprint is significantly smaller.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: THE STRONGEST BRIDGE IN THE DECK. FERC pressed Maine on a 400 acre envelope. Alaska's envelope is 1,650 acres, more than four times as large, and the Alaska deficiency letter as reported did not raise it. State both figures and let the reader see the gap. Do not assert FERC will raise it.

claims.claim: The Eastport City Council voted unanimously to enact a 180 day moratorium that halts all progress on a proposed underwater artificial intelligence data center planned for waters off Eastport.
claims.verbatim: The City Council voted unanimously Wednesday to enact a 180-day moratorium that halts all progress on a proposed underwater artificial intelligence data center planned for waters off Eastport.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: The page says Wednesday and published Thursday August 13th, 2026, so the vote was Wednesday August 12th, 2026. That day is DERIVED, not printed. WABI's August 14th piece is a syndication of this same story, byline and lede identical, so it is NOT an independent second source.

claims.claim: Councilor Karen Raye moved to adopt a moratorium temporarily prohibiting any application, permit, license or approval related to the establishment, construction, expansion or operation of a commercial or industrial data center or artificial intelligence computing facility.
claims.verbatim: application, permit, license or approval related to the establishment, construction, expansion or operation of a commercial or industrial data center or artificial intelligence computing facility.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: The scouts' version of this quote stopped at data center and dropped or artificial intelligence computing facility. The deck must use the full clause.

claims.claim: The Eastport moratorium specifies that facilities on land, underwater, partially or fully submerged, and any co occurring infrastructure are included in the ban.
claims.verbatim: The moratorium specifies that facilities on land, underwater, partially or fully submerged, and any co-occurring infrastructure are included in the ban
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: The page adds that the ban lasts 180 days unless extended or terminated by the council or until the citizen initiated ordinances have been reviewed and decided, so it is not automatically a hard 180 days.

claims.claim: The Maine Monitor reported that the permit application for the Alaska project received a similar letter of deficiencies from FERC but that the company has not indicated the Alaska proposal is being scaled down.
claims.verbatim: The permit application for the Alaska project received a similar letter of deficiencies from FERC, but the company has not indicated that the Alaska proposal is being scaled down.
claims.source_outlet: The Maine Monitor, Melissa S. Razdrih
claims.notes: Verified verbatim and it is the load bearing sentence for the whole deck. It is an absence of indication, not a company denial, so keep the outlet's hedged wording and attribute it on the slide.

claims.claim: A FERC preliminary permit is issued for up to four years for projects in state waters and gives the developer priority to study a project at the specified site for the duration of the permit.
claims.verbatim: issued for up to four years for projects in state waters; gives the developer priority to study a project at the specified site for the duration of the permit.
claims.notes: The permit versus license distinction is nationally true and is the most useful thing on this page. A preliminary permit authorises STUDY, not construction, so nothing here is approved to be built.

claims.claim: A FERC license, unlike a preliminary permit, is granted to construct and operate a hydrokinetic electric generation facility.
claims.verbatim: licenses are granted to construct and operate a hydrokinetic electric generation facility
claims.notes: The page states the term as 30 to 50 years but prints it with an en dash, which house rules bar, so the term is out of the verbatim. If the deck needs it, write 30 to 50 years and attribute.

claims.claim: As of July 15th, 2026 the Northeast Ocean Data Portal counted one licensed marine hydrokinetic project in the Northeast region against five active preliminary permits and two pending applications.
claims.notes: REGION SCOPED and the claim text must say Northeast region every time it is used. There is no national figure available. Weakest claim in the set. Drop it before any other if the deck needs to shed one.

killed.claim: The Maine project was cut by roughly 94 percent
killed.why: This compares a 400 acre operational ENVELOPE to a 27.1 acre active infrastructure FOOTPRINT, which are different quantities. The Quoddy Tides reported on February 27th, 2026 that the ORIGINAL filing already described about 27 acres of active infrastructure inside the 400 acre envelope, roughly 7 percent of the space. The physical footprint barely moved. The verified cuts are capacity, 51 MW to a maximum of 15 MW, and turbines, approximately 170 to 16 plus 34. Both are about 70 percent. Write roughly 70 percent, never 94.

killed.claim: The Alaska application was filed on February 11th, 2026, the same day as the Maine sibling
killed.why: February 11th is sourced only for the MAINE application. No fetched page gives a day for the Alaska filing. Keep February 2026 and no closer.

killed.claim: The Maine project was scaled down in a June 8th, 2026 amendment
killed.why: The Maine Monitor of July 23rd says In July, DeepGreen amended its proposal. No page prints June 8th. Date killed, before and after figures kept in C35, C36 and C37.

killed.claim: The Alaska deficiency letter listed three deficiencies
killed.why: ADN describes the deficiencies but publishes no count for the Alaska letter. Only the Maine letter has a published count, four. Asserting three for Alaska would be the exact merge of the two letters this check exists to prevent.

killed.claim: FERC required notification of municipalities within a 15 mile radius with population over 5,000
killed.why: This threshold appears in no fetched page. A rule nobody can point at is a rule somebody invented.

killed.claim: The Maine DeepGreen project is FERC Project No. P-15424
killed.why: No fetched page publishes it and the Federal Register returns zero DeepGreen documents, so there is no primary docket entry to confirm it against.

killed.claim: The Alaska DeepGreen application carries a FERC project number
killed.why: No source publishes one. The Federal Register count of zero is consistent with no accepted filing and therefore no published docket notice.

killed.claim: The Cook Inlet PowerLink project costs 400 million dollars
killed.why: Barred as a settled figure. AEA's own page says $142 Million, ADN reports $400 million, and a roughly $206 million 2023 federal award is a third figure nobody verified. Kept only as C28, explicitly attributed, beside the primary AEA page in C29.

killed.claim: AEA's board endorsed a 400 million dollar financing package on August 9th, 2026 relevant to this project
killed.why: That endorsement concerns the Bradley Lake expansion, a different project, and no source was fetched for it. Excluded entirely so it can never be blended with the PowerLink cost.

killed.claim: WABI independently confirmed the Eastport vote on August 14th, 2026
killed.why: The WABI page carries the dateline EASTPORT, Maine (THE MAINE MONITOR) and reproduces the Maine Monitor lede word for word. It is a syndication, not corroboration.

killed.claim: The Eastport vote took place on August 14th, 2026
killed.why: Both pages say Wednesday. August 14th, 2026 is a Friday. The Maine Monitor published Thursday August 13th, so the vote was Wednesday August 12th, 2026.

killed.claim: The Cook Inlet proposal includes up to 350 turbines, stated flatly
killed.why: ADN prints as many 350 underwater turbines, which reads as a typo and is a ceiling in any case. The Maine Monitor prints approximately 330 to 350, which is the form kept in C12.

killed.claim: Nationally there are N marine hydrokinetic preliminary permits per license
killed.why: ferc.gov returns 403 to automated fetches and the only counts obtainable are Northeast region scoped. No national ratio may appear on any slide.

killed.claim: Littoral Power Systems holds Project No. P-15317 and Turnagain Arm Tidal Energy holds P-13509
killed.why: The Federal Register title for Littoral carries no P number and no Turnagain Arm document appeared in either search. Unverified, so excluded.

killed.claim: The silt protection is described as engineered scour skirts
killed.why: Phrase order not on the page. ADN prints Silt-protection scour skirts have been engineered. Reworded in C19 to match.
